assumptions: identifiers.org's registry pattern, made fit for running text, is what an accession of that namespace looks like.
limits: Needs the network: the patterns come from identifiers.org and every candidate is resolved at its archive.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which archive records does this text name?

description: Find the sequence accessions a text names (a paper's methods, a notebook, a report) and resolve each against its archive: identifiers.org's own pattern for every namespace a fetch target serves, scanned over the text, then one batched search per archive. A span is listed only when the archive returns a record with that accession, so a catalog number with an accession's shape is reported as unresolved rather than as a hit. Hand `accessions` to fetch_record.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

text.description: the text to scan, e.g. the markdown fetch_article returns.

name: find_accessions

accessions.description: every resolved accession as the text writes it, in text order

found.description: each resolved accession with the record it names (archive, title, organism, length) and how often the text mentions it

namespaces.description: the identifiers.org namespaces read, by prefix and registry name

summary.description: how many accessions resolved, at which archives, and how many spans did not

unresolved.description: spans a pattern admitted that no archive holds
